external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store whose own identity provider vouches for them.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The set of colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for has not been documented.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies colleague group membership changes and leaver information overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight
external_entities.notes: Authentication, exposure, and protection of the HR system are not stated.

external_entities.name: own identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise colleagues' identity provider that vouches for them to the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The provider's permitted colleague population has not been documented.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-in, maintains directory membership, signs tokens, and writes sign-ins to the audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker's second-factor behavior is not documented.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize changing prices and voiding transactions. A store-manager token works against every store because the console does not check store membership.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console's authentication details, exposure, and interface type are not documented.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: The store where the identity broker keeps its signing key.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: Encryption at rest is not documented.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: Encryption at rest is not documented.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: The log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: It is not documented what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether it is encrypted at rest.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token carrying the colleague's staff id and groups.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing the colleague's staff id and group list

data_flows.name: use token
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the issued token to the store admin console, which uses its groups to decide what the colleague may do.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: Token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the broker's signing key to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: store signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs tokens for every application.

data_flows.name: maintain groups
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies overnight group-membership and leaver changes to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group information in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The provider's allowed colleague population is not documented.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: It is not documented what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: own device at home
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing colleagues' own devices at home from which they sign in.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise-controlled zone containing franchise colleagues and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: Colleagues' own devices at home are controlled outside the system's corporate environment.
assumptions.basis: The source describes them as colleagues' 'own devices at home', indicating a different controlling party.

assumptions.assumption: The franchise stores and their identity provider are controlled by a different party from the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly distinguishes 'franchise stores' and says their own identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues.
